# zlib-ng / fuzzer_checksum

zlib-ng's own fuzz target `fuzzer_checksum` ([source](source/fuzzer_checksum.c), unmodified), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over zlib-ng (zlib-ng/zlib-ng at 1579085c).

Checks 6 properties (listed below); the first, an algebraic law: CRC-32 combine law per chunk (chunk size data[0], min 1): crc32_combine_op(crc_so_far, crc32_z(0,chunk), crc32_combine_gen(len)) == crc32_z(crc_so_far, chunk).

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against zlib-ng at commit 1579085c.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- CRC-32 combine law per chunk (chunk size data[0], min 1): crc32_combine_op(crc_so_far, crc32_z(0,chunk), crc32_combine_gen(len)) == crc32_z(crc_so_far, chunk) ([lines 33-40](source/fuzzer_checksum.c#L33-L40)): assert(); confirmed in the binary.
- Chunked crc32_z over the input must equal one-shot crc32_z (exercises zlib-ng's SIMD/folding CRC kernels at arbitrary chunk boundaries) ([lines 41-45](source/fuzzer_checksum.c#L41-L45)): assert(); confirmed in the binary.
- crc32_combine(crc1,crc2,len)==crc32_combine(crc1,crc1,len) and combine_op(crc1,crc2)==combine_op(crc2,crc1): trivially true because crc1 == crc2 was just asserted ([lines 48-56](source/fuzzer_checksum.c#L48-L56)): assert(); confirmed in the binary.
- crc32_combine(crc1, crc2, len) == crc32_combine_op(crc2, crc1, crc32_combine_gen(len)): the two combine APIs agree ([lines 53-59](source/fuzzer_checksum.c#L53-L59)): assert(); confirmed in the binary.
- Chunked adler32_z must equal one-shot adler32_z (SIMD Adler kernels at arbitrary chunk boundaries) ([lines 62-68](source/fuzzer_checksum.c#L62-L68)): assert(); confirmed in the binary.
- adler32_combine(adler1, adler2, len) == adler32_combine(adler1, adler1, len): trivially true since adler1 == adler2 ([lines 71-73](source/fuzzer_checksum.c#L71-L73)): assert(); confirmed in the binary.

A failed check marked as ending the process contradicts every halts statement below, so a proof of one implies them on every input it covers.

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch zlib-ng` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |
|---|---|---:|---|
| plain | `fuzzer_checksum.plain` | 103,208 | `f369d125dcdffea67699234c147efb6906e31ed40aa75321f1b97795bd8c7c65` |
| ubsan | `fuzzer_checksum.ubsan` | 92,448 | `1c69dc77c0d7ca6ba01aa60c0923ab1e19aaea8438b3285f3e72d8b61ea4f5c7` |
| asan | `fuzzer_checksum.asan` | 673,784 | `7a6924aca1caf8a745daea3cc311537df2f5cc54e0d00486d08b5c5958cb76df` |
| asan-ubsan | `fuzzer_checksum.asan-ubsan` | 642,488 | `f570fdef179bc9288d43037f05ad50a7b31ea47337292ae36d66a78ccfd1e6ff` |

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
- asan-ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
